summary.headline: LPG business now losing money too; deeper negative equity: the price still assumes a rescue
summary.text: LAUGFS Gas PLC (LGL.N0000 voting, LGL.X0000 non-voting) runs Sri Lanka's second LPG brand, plus LPG ships, a Hambantota terminal and a Dubai trading arm. The July–September 2026 quarter was much worse: the home LPG business sold below cost (a gross loss of Rs 337mn; operating loss Rs 541mn against a Rs 679mn profit a year earlier), and the group lost Rs 1.54bn (EPS minus Rs 3.99), Rs 2.12bn for the half-year. The report also restates the year to March 2026: the loss to owners is now Rs 4.90bn (EPS minus Rs 12.66), not Rs 3.34bn, and equity at March is minus Rs 2.75bn. Equity to owners has fallen to minus Rs 4.98bn (NAV minus Rs 12.88 a share), and borrowings are Rs 35.7bn (Rs 24.9bn due within a year) against Rs 3.0bn of cash. The voting share closed at Rs 49.40 on 13 November 2026, valuing the equity at about Rs 18.5bn. I'd only buy at up to about Rs 4.80 (strong buy under Rs 4.30), and would avoid it until the debt is dealt with and the LPG business is profitable again.

highlights.title: Three months to 30 September 2026 (unaudited)
highlights.text: Group revenue fell 57% to Rs 5.71bn (the Dubai trading arm again had no sales) and there was a gross loss of Rs 471mn. Loss to owners Rs 1.54bn (EPS minus Rs 3.99 against minus Rs 2.14). The LPG company itself had revenue down 28% to Rs 4.62bn while cost of sales fell only 8%, giving an operating loss of Rs 541mn against a Rs 679mn profit a year earlier. The report doesn't explain why.

highlights.title: Six months to 30 September 2026
highlights.text: Revenue Rs 11.74bn (Rs 25.22bn), loss to owners Rs 2.12bn (Rs 1.15bn), EPS minus Rs 5.48. By segment: LPG loss after tax Rs 1.26bn, shipping Rs 641mn, trading Rs 246mn; property made Rs 36mn. Shipping now has Rs 1.07bn of outside revenue.

highlights.title: Year to March 2026 restated
highlights.text: The new report's year-to-March-2026 column shows a loss to owners of Rs 4.90bn (EPS minus Rs 12.66) and March equity of minus Rs 2.75bn (minus Rs 7.11 a share), against Rs 3.34bn, minus Rs 8.64 and minus Rs 3.06 in the fourth-quarter report. The column is still marked unaudited and the change isn't explained; the audited 2025/26 annual report hasn't been read.

highlights.title: Debt and negative equity
highlights.text: Borrowings Rs 35.7bn at September 2026 (Rs 24.9bn short-term, up from Rs 21.6bn at March) against Rs 3.0bn of cash; the group borrowed a net Rs 1.8bn in the half-year. Equity to owners is minus Rs 4.98bn. Finance costs were Rs 1.45bn in six months.

highlights.title: The share price
highlights.text: The voting share traded between Rs 40 and Rs 54 in July–September 2026 and closed at Rs 49.40 on 13 November. LAUGFS Holdings still owns 74% of the voting shares.

methodReadings.reading: Liabilities exceed assets by more each quarter, even with land, ships and cylinders at revalued amounts.
Losses in five of the last six years and in the first half of this one.
Trailing loss about Rs 15.18 a share; no earnings to value.
The group made an operating loss in the half-year, so interest isn't covered at all; most of the debt is short-term bank loans.

buyPlan.note: About Rs 2,505 in total, against Rs 24,700 at Rs 49.40. I wouldn't buy at all until the debt is refinanced or the ships are sold, and the LPG business is profitable again.
buyPlan.realism: Rs 4.80 needs a fall of about 90%. The lowest voting price in July–September 2026 was Rs 40; the share was about Rs 8 in May 2020, in a crisis. Not realistic unless the company fails or issues many new shares cheaply.

higher: Selling or refinancing the ships so the group debt falls sharply.
A rights issue or parent support that fixes the negative equity.
The LPG business returning to a gross profit (it sold below cost in July–September 2026).
lower: Banks refusing to roll over the Rs 24.9bn of short-term loans.
A going-concern warning in the audited 2025/26 accounts.
A rights issue at a low price that dilutes current shareholders.

notes.disclaimer: These are estimates from the annual reports to March 2024 and March 2025 and the interim reports to September 2026; the audited 2025/26 annual report hasn't been read. The September 2026 interim restates the year to March 2026 (loss to owners Rs 4.90bn instead of Rs 3.34bn) without explaining why; the restated figures are used. The price is the CSE close on 13 November 2026. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.

fullText:
Summary: LAUGFS Gas PLC (LGL.N0000 voting, LGL.X0000 non-voting) runs Sri Lanka's second LPG brand, plus LPG ships, a Hambantota terminal and a Dubai trading arm. The July–September 2026 quarter was much worse: the home LPG business sold below cost (a gross loss of Rs 337mn; operating loss Rs 541mn against a Rs 679mn profit a year earlier), and the group lost Rs 1.54bn (EPS minus Rs 3.99), Rs 2.12bn for the half-year. The report also restates the year to March 2026: the loss to owners is now Rs 4.90bn (EPS minus Rs 12.66), not Rs 3.34bn, and equity at March is minus Rs 2.75bn. Equity to owners has fallen to minus Rs 4.98bn (NAV minus Rs 12.88 a share), and borrowings are Rs 35.7bn (Rs 24.9bn due within a year) against Rs 3.0bn of cash. The voting share closed at Rs 49.40 on 13 November 2026, valuing the equity at about Rs 18.5bn. On a sum of the parts, after debt, the fair value falls to about Rs 5.70 (from Rs 7.90), nil in the bear case. I'd only buy at up to about Rs 4.80 (strong buy under Rs 4.30), and would avoid it until the debt is dealt with and the LPG business is profitable again.

Price and key figures
Price: Rs 49.40 voting, Rs 38.00 non-voting (CSE close, 13 November 2026). In July–September 2026 the voting share traded between Rs 40 and Rs 54 and ended the quarter at Rs 42.60.
Three months to 30 September 2026 (unaudited): group revenue Rs 5.71bn (Rs 13.16bn), gross loss Rs 471mn, operating loss Rs 704mn (profit Rs 12mn), finance costs Rs 789mn, loss to owners Rs 1.54bn (Rs 827mn), EPS minus Rs 3.99 (minus Rs 2.14). The LPG company: revenue Rs 4.62bn (Rs 6.42bn), gross loss Rs 337mn, operating loss Rs 541mn (profit Rs 679mn), loss Rs 1.03bn.
Six months to 30 September 2026: revenue Rs 11.74bn (Rs 25.22bn), loss to owners Rs 2.12bn, EPS minus Rs 5.48 (minus Rs 2.96). Segments after tax: LPG minus Rs 1.26bn, shipping minus Rs 641mn, trading minus Rs 246mn, property Rs 36mn. Operating cash flow minus Rs 1.26bn after interest.
Restated year to March 2026: loss to owners Rs 4.90bn (was Rs 3.34bn), EPS minus Rs 12.66 (was minus Rs 8.64), NAV minus Rs 7.11 (was minus Rs 3.06). The reason isn't given.
Balance sheet, September 2026: borrowings Rs 35.7bn (Rs 24.9bn short-term), cash Rs 3.0bn, equity to owners minus Rs 4.98bn (minus Rs 12.88 a share).

Valuation table (Rs per share)
Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted
Sum of the parts less debt | 0.0 | 1.5 | 21.7 | 5.1
Recovery earnings × P/E | 0.0 | 3.0 | 24.0 | 6.3
Average | 0.0 | 2.3 | 22.9 | 5.7
Fair value about Rs 5.70 (30% bear, 50% base, 20% bull), down from Rs 7.90. Buy at up to Rs 4.80 (15% below); strong buy under Rs 4.30 (25% below).

Assumptions
LPG business worth 5 / 6.5 / 7 times operating cash profit of Rs 1.5 / 2.3 / 3.0bn (cut from Rs 2.0 / 2.8 / 3.2bn: about Rs 3.1bn in 2025/26, but only about Rs 1.6bn over the last 12 months and a cash loss in July–September). Ships and the Hambantota terminal (Rs 17.6bn of segment assets) at 50% / 80% / 90% of book. Investment property Rs 3.8 / 4.2 / 4.2bn. Net debt Rs 32.6bn. After a turnaround: EPS below zero / Rs 0.30 (was Rs 0.50) / Rs 2.00 at 10 / 12 times.

What stands out
- The LPG business, the one part that made money, sold below cost in July–September 2026.
- The year to March 2026 loss was restated Rs 1.56bn worse, without explanation.
- Interest (Rs 1.45bn in six months) is paid from new borrowing; short-term loans rose to Rs 24.9bn.
- The market price still looks like a bet on a rescue, a sale of the ships or a big recovery; none is announced.

500-share plan
200 shares up to Rs 5.70, 150 up to Rs 4.80, 150 up to Rs 4.30: average about Rs 5.01, about Rs 2,505 in total. That needs a fall of about 90%, so it isn't realistic. I'd wait until the debt is dealt with and look again.

What would change my view
Higher: selling or refinancing the ships, a rights issue or parent support that fixes equity, the LPG business back to a gross profit, shipping breaking even.
Lower: banks not rolling over short-term loans, another quarter of LPG losses, more shipping or trading losses, a going-concern warning, a dilutive rights issue.

Business tests: 0 of 4 passed: avoid for now (unchanged).
